newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian regional official stabbed in Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Russian regional official stabbed in Moscow.

text.p: An aide to a Siberian regional governor sacked by President Boris Yeltsin this week was stabbed and badly injured in Moscow on Thursday, police said.

The attack on 27-year-old Dmitry Chirkadze, deputy governor of the depressed coal and steel producing region of Kemerovo, highlighted the turbulent politics of an area which is one of the worst hit by Russia's economic crisis and where Moscow has accused officials of corruption and links to organised crime.
Police said the assailants did not rob Chirkadze, a former aluminium works boss put in charge of industry, transport and communications in February by ex-governor Mikhail Kislyuk.

Yeltsin accused Kislyuk of aggravating the crisis in Kemerovo and sacked him on Tuesday, replacing him with former minister Aman Tuleyev. Tuleyev accused regional leaders of links to mafia-style groups and of misappropriating funds.
Doctors said Chirkadze was in a "rather serious" condition in hospital after being stabbed by two assailants as he left the home of relatives in a Moscow suburb. They also broke his jaw.
Police said they had no immediate clues on their identity.
A senior Yeltsin aide said this week the Kremlin leader, worried by the growing crime rate in Russia, had decided to take the issue to his top policy-making body, the Security Council.
The council's deputy secretary Mikhail Mityukov said on Tuesday that a meeting was likely "in the near future".

"The crime situation has become a key destabilising factor which harms social and economic reforms and threatens national security," Mityukov said. He did not specify when Yeltsin planned to summon the meeting.
Mityukov said the government's failure to curb crime and corruption were feeding public distrust and scepticism about its ability to handle other major problems.
